game.title: All About Wisconsin
game.description: A classroom tour of the Badger State: its history, geography, government and traditions. Suitable for a Wisconsin history or social studies class.

images.description: Photo of the Little White Schoolhouse in Ripon, Wisconsin, a small white one-room wooden schoolhouse.
Outline map of Wisconsin showing its lakes and rivers, with no city names.

questions.prompt: Warm-up: which Wisconsin tradition is your favorite?
A March 1854 meeting in this Ripon schoolhouse is traditionally called the birthplace of which political party?
True or false: Wisconsin's largest city is also its state capital.
When Wisconsin joined the Union in 1848, it became the ___th state. (Answer with a number.)
Which of these are official Wisconsin state symbols? Select all that apply.
Sort each event into the period when it happened.

cards: Jean Nicolet lands on the shore of Green Bay
The Peshtigo Fire, deadliest wildfire in U.S. history
Wisconsin passes the first U.S. unemployment insurance law
Marquette and Jolliet travel the Wisconsin River
The first U.S. kindergarten opens in Watertown
The first Summerfest is held in Milwaukee
The Black Hawk War ends at the Battle of Bad Axe
Wisconsin's Iron Brigade fights in the Civil War

questions.prompt: Find Madison, the state capital, on this map of Wisconsin.
Which Wisconsin U.S. senator founded Earth Day in 1970?
True or false: Wisconsin grows more cranberries than any other state.
Wisconsin's state motto is a single word: ___.
